messages:
Asha (Design): quick sync — putting up a small design review for the latency panel tiling and sampling controls. Goal: make heatmap + p95 tiles scannable at a glance while preserving precise controls for deep-dive. mock: https://img.redwood.local/ux/tiling-v1.png :eyes:

Tom (Eng-Frontend): looks compact. two quick concerns: rendering lots of tiny heatmap tiles kills CPU on low-end machines. can we virtualize or render to canvas instead of DOM cells?

Asha (Design): good call. proposal: canvas for dense view, DOM for expanded single-tile view so screenreader semantics stay intact. also want keyboard navigation between tiles (arrow keys) and logical focus ring.

Samir (Eng-ML): agree on keyboard nav. also: p95 tooltip needs to surface sample-count + samplerate. if we show only p95 number customers assume it’s full population. suggest microcopy: "95th percentile latency (based on N sampled requests, sampling rate X%)"

Miguel (Product): +1. another product ask: easy compare mode — toggle that splits the tile to show current vs previous period. customers want quick compare without opening full chart. could be a small compare icon on tile header.

Tom (Eng-Frontend): for the sampling control, slider feels friendly but is too imprecise for low rates (0.1% vs 0.01%). suggestion: slider + inline numeric input for exact values. slider steps: coarse, hold modifier for fine-grain.

Asha (Design): proposed control: label "Sampling (trace capture rate)"; primary affordance: slider 0–100% with secondary numeric input and presets: [Adaptive, 1%, 0.1%, 0.01%]. helper text: "Controls fraction of requests for which we capture raw traces. Lower rates reduce cost."

Samir (Eng-ML): small example of how backend query will read this, fyi:
```
GET /api/latency?range=1h&samplerate=0.001&tiling=dense
```
We should expose samplerate in the API and show it in the UI so numbers match.

Jo (Accessibility): accessibility nits: color contrast for the heatmap legend fails 3:1 on some low-contrast palettes. add aria-labels on tile toggle buttons and ensure slider is keyboard operable with aria-valuetext showing percent and an accessible name for presets. also: avoid using only color; add intensity labels on hover/focus.

Asha (Design): noted — update palette to WCAG AA for 3:1 and surface a patterned overlay option for color-blind mode. copy tweak: change tooltip header from "p95" to "95th percentile latency" and put the unit on the same line (e.g., "95th percentile latency — 420 ms"). keep parentheses for sample metadata.

Tom (Eng-Frontend): implementation Q: when density toggle is "dense" we hide axis labels to save space. But that breaks discoverability. maybe show compact axis on hover or when tile expanded.

Miguel (Product): prefer small persistent unit label (ms) at bottom-right of tile so people always know what they're looking at.

Asha (Design): agreed. also thinking about time presets language: use full words for accessibility: "Last 30 minutes" not "30m". for localization, keep canonical strings.

Samir (Eng-ML): telemetry: record which sampling preset is in use and whether compare mode was opened. we need that to explain p95 regressions when sample rates change.

Asha (Design): next steps: I'll iterate mocks with canvas-backed dense view, slider+input for samplerate, and compare toggle in tile header. will include alt patterns for colorblind mode and full microcopy for tooltips. @Tom please call out any perf limits (max tiles before we switch to aggregated mode). @Jo can you review the a11y checklist once mocks are up?

Tom (Eng-Frontend): will do. rough perf threshold: ~64 tiles on medium machines before frame drops; prefer to show aggregated overview beyond that and provide a "zoom" to expand subset.

Jo (Accessibility): happy to review — will check keyboard flow + screenreader strings when ready.

Miguel (Product): thanks all. if we can get a compact mock by EOD tomorrow, we can show to 1:1 customers next week. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: deploy scheduled for staging at 2028-06-12T03:00Z — include flag: feature.latency-tiling-v1

Asha (Design): great — will attach final mocks here when done. thanks! :sparkles:
